}}'''Denis Jérome''' (born 28 February 1939 in Paris) is a French experimental [[physicist]] in the field of condensed matter, who contributed to the discovery of [[superconductivity]] in organic conductive matter.

== Career ==
He studied at the [[Sorbonne University|Sorbonne]], where he obtained his bachelor's degree in science in 1960, then the diploma of advanced studies in solid-state physics. In 1965, he obtained his [[Doctor of Science|doctorate in science]] under the supervision of Professor [[Anatole Abragam]] at the [[University of Paris-Saclay]].

From 1965 to 1966, he worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|post-doctoral]] fellow at the [[University of California]] at [[San Diego]], in the laboratory of Professor [[Walter Kohn]], winner of the 1998 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, where he conducted research in collaboration with Professor T. M. Rice. He then continued his post-doctoral research at [[Harvard University]] until March 1967.

In October 1962, he joined the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|Centre national de recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) as a research intern. He successively became a research master in 1970, research director in 1980, and director of research emeritus of the CNRS in 2004.

In 1967, he formed the "study group on the electronic properties of metals and alloys under very high [[hydrostatic pressure]] and low temperature" at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] at the request of Professors [[Jacques Friedel]] and [[André Guinier]].

He is a specialist in the physics of low-dimensional electrons and the [[Metal–insulator transition|metal-insulator transition]], known as Nevill Mott's transition.

His major contribution to scientific knowledge is the discovery, in 1980, in cooperation with Professor [[Klaus Bechgaard]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Klaus Bechgaard|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-B/klaus-bechgaard.html|date=}}</ref> of the phenomenon of superconductivity in the organic solid with the detection of superconductivity at 0.9 K under a pressure of 12 kbar in Bechgaard salt (TMTSF)<sub>2</sub>PF<sub>6</sub>.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Organic Superconductors|journal=Scholarpedia|volume=10|issue=1|article-number=30655|language=en |date=2015-01-14|doi=10.4249/scholarpedia.30655|last1=Jerome|first1=Denis|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He has also contributed to the study of low-dimensional conductors, organic or inorganic, through various measurements of electronic properties under high pressure. He has published more than 390 scientific articles in international journals and several journal articles, book chapters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.fr/scholar?start=0&q=Denis+J%C3%A9rome&hl=fr&as_sdt=0,5|title=Google scholar}}</ref> and in 2024 a retrospective on low dimensional [[organic conductor]]s and superconductors.

He has been chief editor of several international scientific journals, Journal de Physique Lettres, [[Journal de Physique]], [[European Physical Journal]] B and [[Europhysics Letters]].

Within the framework of the French Academy of Sciences, of which he is a member in the Physics section,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-J/denis-jerome.html|title=Académie des sciences|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411171608/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-J/denis-jerome.html |archive-date=2016-04-11 }}</ref> he coordinated the drafting of reports on the individual evaluation of researchers and teacher-researchers in the exact and experimental sciences in 2009, on the proper use of bibliometry{{sfn|Bach|Jérome|2011|p=5}} in 2011 and on the new challenges of scientific publishing{{sfn|Bach|Jérome|2014|p=5}} in 2014. He was President of the Physics section of the French Academy of Sciences from 2011 to 2015. He led a symposium on the interface between physics and chemistry<ref>{{cite web|title=Interface Physique Chimie|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Colloques-conferences-et-debats-par-et-pour-la-communaute-scientifique/a-l-interface-de-la-chimie-et-de-la-physique.html|date=}}</ref> in February 2013 and on the physics of condensed matter in the 21st century<ref>{{cite web|title=La physique de la matière condensée au 21eme siècle|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Colloques-conferences-et-debats/physique-de-la-matiere-condensee-au-21e-siecle-l-impact-de-jacques-friedel.html|date=}}</ref> in January 2016.

== Distinctions ==

=== Prizes ===

*    Bronze medal CNRS, 1965
*    Laureate of the French Academy of Sciences (Doistaut-Blutel Prize), 1980
*    [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize|Holweck Prize]] of the [[Société Française de Physique|French Physical Society]] and [[Institute of Physics]], 1985
*    French Outreach Committee Award, 1990
*    [[Hewlett-Packard|Hewlett Packard]] Europhysics Prize of the [[European Physical Society]] 1991, with Klaus Bechgaard for the discovery of organic superconduction
*    Kelvin Lecturer, Society of Electrical Engineers in London, 1984
*    Regent's Professor, University of California, [[Los Angeles]], November 1992       

=== Member of learned societies ===

*    French Physical Society
*    European Physical Society, Fellow of the European Physical Society
*    Member of the French Academy of Sciences since 2005<ref name=":0" />

=== Doctorates Honoris Causa and distinctions ===

*    Doctor Honoris Causa of the [[Université de Sherbrooke]] and Speaker [[Walter Kohn]], Canada, June 2005 
*    Doctor Honoris Causa from the [[University of Stuttgart]], Germany, November 2005 
*    Fellow of the European Physical Society, October 2008     

=== Decorations ===

*    Officier in the [[Ordre national du Mérite|Ordre National du Mérite]], November 2008   
*    Chevalier in the Ordre of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'honneur]], July 2016

== Family ==
Denis Jerome is the grandson of architect [[Lucien Bechmann]] who built part of the [[Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris|Cité Universitaire]] in Paris and the great grandson of Polytechnicien et [[Ingénieur des ponts et chaussées|ingénieur des Ponts et Chaussées]] Georges Bechmann who contributed to the construction of the North-South metro line in [[Paris]] and the construction of the sanitation network.
